liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **What You See** (1 review, 1 other source): John Scofield played guitar on What You See; What You See and Hottentot with Scofield sitting in were singled out as standout moments [2][3]
- **Steppin'** (1 other source): Steppin' flows into Bad Boys For Life and then returns to Steppin' [1]
- **Nuthin' But a** (1 other source): Jesus Children leads into Stay, then Nuthin' But a "G" Thang, before returning to Stay and Jesus Children [1]
- **Bad Boys For Life** (1 other source): Talib Kweli joined on vocals for Bad Boys For Life [2]
- **Uncle Jr** (1 review): Uncle Jr featured some striking clavinet solos from Neal [3]
- **Azucar** (1 review): Disc 2 track 1 combines Azucar and Uncle Jr into a single track [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **soulive2004-01-17d1t01**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **soulive2004-01-17d1t02**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **soulive2004-01-17d1t03**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **soulive2004-01-17d1t04**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **soulive2004-01-17d1t05**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **soulive2004-01-17d1t06**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **soulive2004-01-17d1t07**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **soulive2004-01-17d1t08**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **soulive2004-01-17.mbho.shn** (recommended): source not stated; 14 songs; 115 min; rated 4/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: The mbho recording has better-balanced drums and much better vocals; The mbho copy captures Talib's freestyle well; The mbho recording has better frequency range, though its track splits are off [8][11][14]
- **Soulive04-01-17.shnf**: source not stated; 13 songs; 116 min; rated 3.88/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Vocals are inaudible and muddy in the first few songs, and the high end sounds flat; Drums sound distant and the recording sounds cave-like; the on-stage approach suits this band poorly; This source has better-balanced drums and much better vocals than Rak's on-stage pull [7][9]

## Around the show

- The night was a dual headline bill with the John Scofield Band [2]
- John Scofield sat in with Soulive during this show [4]
- The setlist was better than those of the previous two tours [7]
- Reviewer prefers this recording to Rak's on-stage pull of the same show [8]
- Reviewer prefers this recording to Rak's on-stage pull; the show didn't suit on-stage taping [9]
- Reviewer says on-stage mic recordings suit this show less than the mbho copy, despite Rak's strong pulls [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **soulive2004-01-17.mbho.shn**: taped by Ian Stone; transferred by Ian Stone; source: MBHO ka200n/603a > MP2 > AD2K+ > digigram vxpocket/lifebookP2120 > wavlab4 @ 24/48 > wav [1]
- **Soulive04-01-17.shnf**: taped by Andrew Rakow; transferred by Andrew Rakow; source: Neumann AK40 (onstage, xy, right center) > LC3KA > KM100 > Lunatec V2 > Apogee AD1000 > Tascam DA-P1 @ 44.1 [2]. Also: The taper also recorded Scofield's guest set from the stage, but it isn't on the archive [3]
